The conflict: register says "Cardinal Scale Manufacturing Co.", document says "Cardinal Scale Manufacturing Company".

"Co." is an abbreviation of "Company". This is a classic legal-suffix drift / abbreviation — same entity. Per rules, spelling drift, legal-suffix drift = same-entity. Best value: which one? For same-entity, typically the register's canonical form... but actually the rules say for number/year format differences use register's canonical form. For same-entity in general, best value — the register's canonical form seems safest, but "Company" spelled out is arguably more complete/accurate from the legal instrument. Hmm.

The rules specify best_value only explicitly for document-noise (register), different-entity (document), and number/year same-entity (register canonical). For general same-entity, convention in fusion is register canonical form. "Co." vs "Company" — both acceptable. I'd pick the register's canonical form "Cardinal Scale Manufacturing Co." to maintain consistency with register as canonical source, or the fuller "Company" since document is legal instrument. The rules say "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." That suggests same-entity defaults to register canonical form. So best_value = "Cardinal Scale Manufacturing Co.".

Verdict: same-entity.
